Thank you, Chair Donauer. On April 9th, Betty Lillian Wright passed away at the age of 94. Betty was a formidable citizen in her own right and also the wife of the late Cliff Wright, who was the mayor of Saskatoon from 1976 to 1988.
At the time, the longest serving mayor in our city. Her family writes in the early 1940s, Betty's family moved to Saskatoon from Regina.

This was a very faithful move. As Saskatoon was where she met the love of her life cliff, and where they would marry, raise a family, and contribute to the community that they both loved throughout their lives.
We would remain in awe of their 70 year devotion to each other.
Mom once invited with a hint of embarrassment that she had gone to a party as the date of someone else, but connected there with Cliff and ended up leaving with them.
What could I do? She said, I knew immediately the cliff was the one and that was that.

Betty Wright was a lifelong learner and a passionate supporter of her family and community. She even went to university to complete her bachelor degree at the same time as her children started university.
The family says the house often looked more like a school than a conventional home. The walls were festooned with maps.
Lists of historical facts, diagrams of dynasties, wise quotes such as Thoros, a different drummer.
When her grandson was born, she was so excited that she called Denny Carr, from the wall in Den Show on C.F.K.C. radio, who promptly reported this important civic news.
Today, that grandchild, Duncan, says her dedication to teaching us the joys of life and skills such as how to drive a standard car for just special bond.
Betty had 17 great grandchildren. Betty genuinely liked everybody, looking beyond imperfections, always focusing on the good.
In the world we live in today, I am grateful for Betty's example as she reminds us all the kindness matters.
I'll leave the last words to the family. We have said from time to time, only partly tongue and cheek, that our successes in life are attributable to having chosen our parents brilliantly.
We cannot believe our good luck and will be forever grateful for mom and dad.
